How do you care for a ZZ plant in the UAE?

ZZ plant care in the UAE is simple: keep the plant indoors in bright indirect light, away from direct sun through glass, and water only when the soil is completely dry to the bottom of the pot. A ZZ plant (Zamioculcas zamiifolia) stores water in its underground rhizomes, so too much water, not too little, causes most problems.

Zamioculcas zamiifolia · Also called Zanzibar gem, Aroid palm, Emerald palm, Eternity plant, Zuzu plant, زاميوكولكاس
By the PlantsWorld team · Updated 12 November 2026

ZZ Plant quick facts

LightBright indirect is best; tolerates low light and office lighting. Direct sun scorches the leaves.
WaterOnly when the soil is completely dry to the bottom of the pot. Check the soil, not the calendar.
SoilCoarse, fast-draining mix in a pot with a drainage hole.
TemperatureKeep above 60 °F, about 16 °C (Clemson Extension). A normal AC room suits it.
HumidityAdapts to normal indoor humidity; no misting needed.
Outdoors in UAEBest kept indoors all year: summer heat and sun and cool winter nights are outside its comfort range.
FeedingVery little: a dilute balanced fertiliser in the growing season only.
PetsToxic to cats and dogs if chewed; keep away from pets and young children.
Size indoorsAbout 60–120 cm; dwarf 'Zenzi' about 25–30 cm.
GrowthSlow.

Is a ZZ plant right for you?

A good fit if

  • You are new to plants, or you travel and sometimes forget to water.
  • Your room has low or medium light, or only office lighting.
  • Your home or office runs AC for most of the year.
  • You want a glossy, upright plant that grows slowly and keeps its shape.

Think twice if

  • A cat, a dog or a young child in your home chews plants: ZZ plants are toxic if eaten.
  • You like to water often, or your pots have no drainage hole.
  • You want a plant for a sunny balcony or fast growth.

How much light does a ZZ plant need?

A ZZ plant grows best in bright, indirect light, but it also grows in deep shade and under fluorescent office lighting. A ZZ plant tolerates low light, but UConn notes that it grows much more slowly there.

Direct sun is the main light risk for a ZZ plant in the UAE. Strong sun scalds the leaves: they turn whitish or brown and can curl. Keep a ZZ plant out of afternoon sun behind west- or south-facing glass. A sheer curtain, or a spot a little back from the window, gives bright light without the scorch.

  • Test the spot at the brightest time of day. Iowa State Extension describes bright indirect light as light that is bright enough to cast a distinct shadow, with no sun rays on the leaves. If sun falls straight on the leaves, the spot gets direct sun.

How often should you water a ZZ plant in Dubai and the UAE?

Water a ZZ plant only when the soil is completely dry, all the way to the bottom of the pot. A ZZ plant stores water in its thick underground rhizomes and is highly drought tolerant, so a missed watering does little harm, but soil that stays wet rots the rhizomes.

There is no fixed schedule that suits every home. Test the soil instead: push a wooden skewer to the bottom of the pot and pull it out. If it comes out damp or with soil stuck to it, wait and test again later. You can also lift the pot: a pot with dry soil feels clearly lighter than just after watering.

How fast a ZZ plant's soil dries depends on the home. Small pots, terracotta pots, bright spots and warm rooms dry faster. Large plastic or glazed pots, dim rooms, cool AC rooms and humid coastal homes dry more slowly. In winter, when growth slows, the soil stays wet for longer.

Extension services give only rough guides: NC State Extension suggests watering about twice a month in summer and about once a month in winter, in both cases only if the soil has dried out completely. Use the soil test before every watering, not the number.

When you water a ZZ plant, water thoroughly until water runs out of the drainage hole. Let the pot drain fully before you put it back in a decorative pot or on a saucer, and do not leave it standing in water.

  • When in doubt, wait. UConn advises you to err on the dry side: overwatering is just about the only thing that kills this tough plant.

What soil and pot does a ZZ plant need?

A ZZ plant needs a coarse, fast-draining mix, because it does not tolerate wet roots. Clemson Extension suggests half peat- or coir-based potting soil, a quarter perlite and a quarter sand. A cactus and succulent soil, or potting soil mixed with perlite, also drains well.

Always use a pot with a drainage hole for a ZZ plant. A decorative pot without a hole is fine as an outer cover if you lift the inner pot out to drain after watering.

Should you fertilise a ZZ plant?

Yes, but a ZZ plant needs very little fertiliser, and extension services do not agree on how much. NC State suggests a balanced fertiliser only once or twice a year, and Clemson and UConn once or twice in the growing season (UConn: at half strength). Iowa State and Illinois Extension suggest a light or dilute feed once or twice a month in spring and summer.

A safe middle way for a ZZ plant is a balanced fertiliser at half strength, only while the plant is making new stems, and no feeding when growth stops. UConn notes that ZZ plants grow much more slowly in the low light of many homes, so a plant in a dim spot needs less.

When and how should you repot a ZZ plant?

Repot a ZZ plant when the rhizomes and roots fill the pot: roots grow out of the drainage hole, new stems push against the sides, or the soil dries out much faster than it used to. UConn notes that the stems of a ZZ plant left too long in one pot can push out and crack the sides of the pot.

Move a ZZ plant into the next pot size up, not a much bigger one. UConn notes that a pot too big for the root system holds more water than the roots can use, and the plant then shows signs of overwatering.

Repot a ZZ plant while it is actively growing (Illinois Extension). In the UAE, autumn (October–November) and spring (March–April) avoid both the summer heat and the winter slowdown. A new ZZ plant does not need repotting unless it shows the signs of a full pot.

  1. Choose a pot one size up, with a drainage hole, and fresh fast-draining mix.
  2. Ease the plant out of the old pot. Squeeze or tap a plastic pot to loosen the root ball; cut a cracked pot away.
  3. Shake off the loose old soil and check the rhizomes. Cut away any that are soft and brown.
  4. Set the plant at the same depth as before, fill around it with the new mix and press it down gently.
  5. Water lightly, let the pot drain fully, and then wait until the soil is dry before the next watering.

How do you propagate a ZZ plant?

Division is the most common and fastest way to propagate a ZZ plant, because each piece already has its own rhizome. Leaf cuttings also work and give more new plants, but they are slow: UConn reports that small rhizomes form in about a month in a greenhouse, and that indoors it may take up to nine months.

For ZZ plant leaf cuttings, take whole leaves or the top part of a leaf stem; Illinois Extension reports that cuttings from the top of the leaf gave the most new rhizomes, and that a stem piece without a leaf did not root. Let the cut ends dry and seal before you plant them (UConn: a few hours; Illinois Extension: a few days), then set them in damp, free-draining potting mix in a warm, bright spot out of direct sun.

  1. Take the plant out of its pot and shake off the loose soil.
  2. Pull or cut the rhizome clump apart with a clean knife so each piece has stems, roots and its own rhizome.
  3. Pot each piece in its own pot of fast-draining mix, at the same depth as before.
  4. Water lightly, let it drain, then care for each piece as a normal ZZ plant.

Where should you put a ZZ plant at home or in the office?

A ZZ plant suits bedrooms, hallways, living-room corners, office desks and reception areas, because it tolerates low light and office lighting. It is widely used in commercial interiors for that reason.

Do not put a ZZ plant in the direct cold airflow from an AC vent, next to a sunny glass wall, or on a balcony. ZZ plants are sensitive to cold, so in winter also keep them away from cold windows and doors in inland homes. Tall ZZ plants make good floor plants; the dwarf 'Zenzi' and young plants suit shelves and desks.

What should you do in the first week after your ZZ plant arrives?

A new ZZ plant needs time to settle in. The main risk in the first week is too much water, not too little.

  1. Put the plant in bright indirect light, away from direct sun and from the airflow of AC vents.
  2. Do the skewer test before you water. The soil from the nursery is often still damp.
  3. Do not repot it straight away. Repot only when it shows the signs in the repotting section.

How does ZZ plant care change through the UAE year?

Summer May–Sep

Keep the ZZ plant indoors in an AC room, out of direct sun through glass. Soil in a warm, bright spot can dry faster than in winter, so use the skewer test before every watering. Feed at half strength only while the plant makes new stems.

Autumn Oct–Nov

Autumn is a good time to repot or divide a ZZ plant that fills its pot. Water only when the soil is dry; as rooms cool, the soil dries more slowly.

Winter Dec–Feb

Growth often slows in winter (NC State), so the soil can stay wet for longer: test before you water, and stop feeding while there are no new stems. Winter nights on the coast are mild, but inland (Al Ain, desert areas) and in Riyadh or Kuwait, nights can be cold. Keep ZZ plants away from cold windows, doors and draughts, and above about 16 °C.

Spring Mar–Apr

When a ZZ plant makes new stems in spring, start feeding again at half strength. Spring is the second good window to repot or divide a ZZ plant before the summer heat.

What are common ZZ plant problems and how do you fix them?

What you seeLikely causeFirst step
Yellow leaves, soft stems at the baseOverwatering and rhizome rotStop watering.
Whitish, pale or brown dry patches, curling leavesSun scaldMove the plant out of direct sun, or add a sheer curtain to the window.
Dark spots or streaks on the stemsNormal stem markingsPress the stem gently. If it is firm, do nothing.
Brown bumps, white fluff or sticky leavesScale insects or mealybugsMove the plant away from other plants.
No new stems for a long timeLow light, cool season or normal slow growthMove the plant to brighter indirect light; Clemson Extension notes that this speeds up growth.

Why are my ZZ plant leaves turning yellow, and how do I save it from rhizome rot?

Yellow ZZ plant leaves with soft stems at the base are the usual sign of overwatering. When the soil stays wet, the rhizomes start to rot and can no longer feed the leaves.

How to tell: Soil still damp long after watering, a ring of soft brown or black tissue where the stems meet the soil, and soft, brown rhizomes and roots.

How to fix it:

  1. Stop watering.
  2. Take the plant out of the pot and remove the wet soil.
  3. Cut away every soft, brown rhizome, root and stem with a clean knife. Keep only firm tissue.
  4. Let the cut surfaces dry and seal before you repot.
  5. Repot in fresh, fast-draining mix in a clean pot with a drainage hole.
  6. Water again only when the new soil is dry to the bottom of the pot.
  7. If no firm rhizome is left, start new plants from healthy leaves (see propagation).

What are the white, pale or brown patches on my ZZ plant leaves?

Whitish, pale or brown patches on ZZ plant leaves, sometimes with curling, are sun scald from direct sun. In the UAE this often happens behind west- or south-facing glass, or after a move to a sunnier spot.

How to tell: Damage on the side that faces the window or the sun.

How to fix it:

  1. Move the plant out of direct sun, or add a sheer curtain to the window.
  2. Leave the marked leaves, or cut badly damaged leaves off at the base.

Are black spots on ZZ plant stems a problem?

Dark spots on firm ZZ plant stems are normal. Clemson Extension notes that a stem with these spots is a typical, healthy ZZ plant.

How to tell: Spots on firm, upright stems with healthy leaves. Soft, mushy, dark stems at the soil line are different: that is rot.

How to fix it:

  1. Press the stem gently. If it is firm, do nothing.
  2. If the stem is soft at the base, follow the rhizome rot fix for yellow leaves.

What are the bumps or white fluff on my ZZ plant?

Small brown bumps on the stems and leaves of a ZZ plant are usually scale insects; white, cottony clusters are mealybugs. ZZ plants have few pest problems, but they can get scale, mealybugs, aphids, thrips and whiteflies.

How to tell: Bumps that scrape off, white fluff, sticky residue on the leaves or the floor.

How to fix it:

  1. Move the plant away from other plants.
  2. Scrape scale off with a fingernail. Wipe mealybugs off with a cotton bud dipped in rubbing alcohol (Clemson Extension).
  3. If they come back, use an insecticidal soap or a neem-based product, follow the label, and expect to repeat the treatment.

Helps: Neem Shield – Herbal Pesticide

Why is my ZZ plant not growing?

ZZ plants grow very slowly and in spurts (Iowa State Extension), and much more slowly in low light (UConn) or in winter. As long as the stems are firm and the leaves are green, a long pause is normal.

How to tell: No new stems, but firm, glossy existing leaves.

How to fix it:

  1. Move the plant to brighter indirect light; Clemson Extension notes that this speeds up growth.
  2. Feed lightly at half strength in spring and summer.
  3. Check that the pot is not packed with rhizomes; repot if it is.

ZZ Plant myths and facts

MythFact
A ZZ plant cleans the air in your home.The studies that showed potted plants removing chemicals used small sealed test chambers. A 2019 review found that a building would need 10 to 1,000 plants per square metre of floor to match normal ventilation.
Touching a ZZ plant is dangerous.NC State Extension lists the ZZ plant as toxic if eaten, but it does not cause skin rashes. The risk is to pets and children that chew the leaves.
Black spots on the stems mean the plant is diseased.Dark spots on firm stems are normal on a healthy ZZ plant. Only soft, mushy stems at the soil line are a sign of rot.
A ZZ plant needs water every week.A ZZ plant stores water in its rhizomes and needs water only when the soil is completely dry.

Is a ZZ plant safe for cats and dogs?

No, a ZZ plant is not safe for cats and dogs: the ASPCA lists the ZZ plant among plants that contain insoluble calcium oxalate crystals. If a pet chews ZZ plant leaves, the crystals can cause drooling, pawing at the mouth, nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea. The ASPCA rates the severity of this group as low and NC State Extension rates the ZZ plant as medium; rarely, a large amount causes throat swelling and difficulty breathing. Keep a ZZ plant out of reach of pets and young children.

If your pet chewed it: Call your vet or a 24-hour animal emergency clinic straight away and tell them the plant name. Do not wait for symptoms. If your pet has trouble swallowing or breathing, take it to a vet hospital at once.

ZZ Plant FAQs

Can a ZZ plant live in a room with no window?

Yes, a ZZ plant can live in a room with no window if the room has electric light for several hours each day. UConn notes that a ZZ plant suits even a windowless office if it gets fluorescent light for several hours a day, and NC State notes that it grows very slowly in such low light.

Does a ZZ plant clean the air?

A ZZ plant does not noticeably clean the air in a normal room. Studies that found plants removing chemicals used small sealed chambers, and a 2019 review found that a building would need 10 to 1,000 plants per square metre of floor to match normal ventilation. Buy a ZZ plant because it looks good and is easy to keep.

Can a ZZ plant live outside in the UAE?

Treat a ZZ plant as an indoor plant in the UAE. UConn gives a range of about 13–27 °C (55–80 °F) and Clemson says to keep it above 60 °F (about 16 °C). UAE summer days and nights are hotter than that range, and inland winter nights can be colder. Direct sun also scalds the leaves.

Is it safe to touch a ZZ plant?

Yes, a ZZ plant is safe to touch. NC State Extension lists the ZZ plant as toxic if eaten, but not as a cause of skin rashes. Keep it where pets and young children cannot chew the leaves.

How long does a ZZ plant leaf cutting take to grow?

A ZZ plant leaf cutting takes a long time to grow. UConn reports that small rhizomes form at the base of a leaf in about a month in a greenhouse, but indoors it may take up to nine months. Illinois Extension notes that roots come first, then a small rhizome.

How fast does a ZZ plant grow?

A ZZ plant grows slowly. Extension services describe the ZZ plant as slow-growing; Iowa State notes that it grows in spurts, and UConn that it grows much more slowly in low light. Over time, most plants reach about 60–120 cm.

Does a ZZ plant flower?

A ZZ plant flowers rarely. A ZZ plant flower is a cream or brown spike (spadix) inside a light green hood (spathe), on a short stalk low down among the bases of the leaf stems. UConn notes that flowers sometimes appear in late summer.

Is a ZZ plant good for an office?

Yes. A ZZ plant tolerates low light, office lighting and missed waterings, and it is one of the most common plants in commercial interiors. Keep it out of the direct airflow from AC vents.

Ordering from PlantsWorld

How is plant size measured?

Size is measured from the bottom of the nursery pot to the top tip of the highest leaf. A plant listed as 50-60 CM stands in that range measured this way.

Which pot option should I choose, nursery or decorative?

Choose the nursery pot for the lowest price or if you already have a planter. Choose a decorative pot for a ready-to-display plant that arrives fully potted with soil mix, perlite and a drainage layer. The plant itself is the same.

Do the decorative pots have drainage holes?

Decorative pot orders include a drainage layer at the base, with premium soil mix and perlite. For specific details on a particular pot model, send us the product link and our team will confirm.

Is the plant healthy on arrival? Can I check first?

Plants are guaranteed to arrive healthy. Check your plant with the delivery agent: if it's damaged or not what you ordered, you can refuse it on the spot. If you find damage after unpacking, send photos and your order number on WhatsApp (+971 4 294 1422) or email sales@plantsworld.ae within 24 hours and we'll replace it free. You can also ask for a pre-dispatch photo.

Will my plant be safe in the UAE heat during delivery?

Yes. Our own delivery team brings your order, not a third-party courier. In extreme summer heat (June to September) we may move deliveries to farther emirates to a cooler day and agree the new day with you. If anything arrives damaged, we replace it free.

My plant arrived with a few drooping or yellow leaves. Is that normal?

Yes, that's normal. A few drooping, bent or yellow leaves are a common reaction to the journey and a new spot, and plants usually recover within a few days. Keep it in bright indirect light and check the soil before watering. If the plant or pot is actually damaged, send photos within 24 hours.

Do I need to repot my plant when it arrives?

Not immediately. Let it settle for a few weeks first, and note that a repotted plant can't be returned or replaced, so check it's healthy before you repot. Plants in decorative pots arrive fully potted. Repot only when roots fill the pot or growth stops.

Something looks wrong with your plant?

Send us photos on WhatsApp and our team will tell you what is happening and what to do. These five photos help us answer fast:

  1. The whole plant, from a step back
  2. A close-up of the problem leaf, front and back
  3. The soil surface and the pot, with the drainage hole if there is one
  4. Where the plant stands: the window, the AC vent and the light
  5. When you last watered, and how much
